exposure: patient and delivery characteristics (type of cesarean delivery, placental complication, blood loss volume)
outcome: severe maternal morbidity (SMM) events contributed by obstetric hemorrhage
cohort: The cohort consists of 193 obstetric hemorrhage events leading to severe maternal morbidity identified in hospitals participating in SMM surveillance in Maryland between August 1, 2020, and December 31, 2022.
finding: Approximately one-third (34.2%) of severe maternal morbidity events contributed by obstetric hemorrhages were deemed preventable, with uterine atony being the leading cause.
mod_finding: Patients with preventable obstetric hemorrhage were significantly more likely to have an emergency compared to a planned cesarean delivery.
